title: Jñānaprasthāna
alt_titles: Aṣṭagrantha / Ba jiandu lun 八犍度論 (T1543)

attribution.tradition: Composed by Kātyāyanīputra (Yaśomitra; Xuanzang); regarded as the 'body' (śarīra) of the Abhidharma, the other six being its 'feet'
attribution.scholarly: Accepted as the central Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma treatise

tradition.text: Three hundred years after the parinirvāṇa (Xuanzang)

structure.description: Eight sections (skandhaka/grantha): miscellaneous, fetters, knowledge, action, great elements, faculties, concentration, views. T1544: 20 fascicles (Xuanzang, 657–660); T1543: 30 fascicles (Saṅghadeva and Zhu Fonian, 383).

summary: The root treatise of the Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma, commented on by the Mahāvibhāṣā. It analyses the fetters, knowledges, actions, elements, faculties, concentrations and views, and states the Abhidharma definition of the word of the Buddha as speech (Yaśomitra's quotation).

title: Prakaraṇapāda
alt_titles: Pinlei zu lun 品類足論 (T1542)
Zhong shifen apitan lun 眾事分阿毘曇論 (T1541)

attribution.scholarly: Attribution to disciples of the Buddha is traditional; the works are dated by scholars to c. 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE

structure.description: Eight chapters; T1542 18 fascicles (Xuanzang, 659); T1541 12 fascicles (Guṇabhadra and Bodhiyaśas, 5th c.)

summary: One of the six 'feet'; systematizes the dharmas into five groups (rūpa, citta, caitasika, cittaviprayukta, asaṃskṛta) — the classification later canonized in the seventy-five dharmas.
notes: Yaśomitra's list (Sphuṭārthā on AK 1.3, checked locally): Jñānaprasthāna – Kātyāyanīputra; Prakaraṇapāda – Vasumitra; Vijñānakāya – Devaśarman; Dharmaskandha – Śāriputra; Prajñaptiśāstra – Maudgalyāyana; Dhātukāya – Pūrṇa; Saṅgītiparyāya – Mahākauṣṭhila. Chinese attributions differ.

title: Vijñānakāya
alt_titles: Apidamo shishen zu lun 阿毘達磨識身足論 (T1539)

attribution.scholarly: Attribution to disciples of the Buddha is traditional; the works are dated by scholars to c. 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE

structure.description: Six chapters; 16 fascicles (Xuanzang, 649)

summary: One of the six 'feet'. Opens by refuting the monk Maudgalyāyana's denial of past and future and a doctrine of the person (pudgala), then analyses consciousness and its conditions (low confidence on the chapter contents).
notes: Yaśomitra's list (Sphuṭārthā on AK 1.3, checked locally): Jñānaprasthāna – Kātyāyanīputra; Prakaraṇapāda – Vasumitra; Vijñānakāya – Devaśarman; Dharmaskandha – Śāriputra; Prajñaptiśāstra – Maudgalyāyana; Dhātukāya – Pūrṇa; Saṅgītiparyāya – Mahākauṣṭhila. Chinese attributions differ.

title: Dharmaskandha
alt_titles: Apidamo fayun zu lun 阿毘達磨法蘊足論 (T1537)

attribution.scholarly: Attribution to disciples of the Buddha is traditional; the works are dated by scholars to c. 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE

structure.description: 21 chapters; 12 fascicles (Xuanzang, 659); Sanskrit fragments from Gilgit (ed. Dietz 1984)

summary: One of the six 'feet', held to be among the oldest: an analysis of the training rules, the fruits, the noble lineages, the right efforts, the bases of power, the applications of mindfulness, the truths, the meditations, the formless states, the faculties, the aggregates and dependent origination, closely comparable to the Pali Vibhaṅga.
notes: Yaśomitra's list (Sphuṭārthā on AK 1.3, checked locally): Jñānaprasthāna – Kātyāyanīputra; Prakaraṇapāda – Vasumitra; Vijñānakāya – Devaśarman; Dharmaskandha – Śāriputra; Prajñaptiśāstra – Maudgalyāyana; Dhātukāya – Pūrṇa; Saṅgītiparyāya – Mahākauṣṭhila. Chinese attributions differ.

title: Prajñaptiśāstra

attribution.scholarly: Attribution to disciples of the Buddha is traditional; the works are dated by scholars to c. 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE

structure.description: Three parts in Tibetan (cosmology, causes, karma); a partial Chinese version in 7 fascicles (T1538, 11th c.)

summary: One of the six 'feet': designations concerning the world (cosmology), the causes (e.g. of a Buddha's marks) and karma.
notes: Yaśomitra's list (Sphuṭārthā on AK 1.3, checked locally): Jñānaprasthāna – Kātyāyanīputra; Prakaraṇapāda – Vasumitra; Vijñānakāya – Devaśarman; Dharmaskandha – Śāriputra; Prajñaptiśāstra – Maudgalyāyana; Dhātukāya – Pūrṇa; Saṅgītiparyāya – Mahākauṣṭhila. Chinese attributions differ.

title: Dhātukāya
alt_titles: Apidamo jieshen zu lun 阿毘達磨界身足論 (T1540)

attribution.scholarly: Attribution to disciples of the Buddha is traditional; the works are dated by scholars to c. 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE

structure.description: 3 fascicles (Xuanzang, 663)

summary: One of the six 'feet': classifies the mental factors and their association and dissociation, comparable in method to the Pali Dhātukathā.
notes: Yaśomitra's list (Sphuṭārthā on AK 1.3, checked locally): Jñānaprasthāna – Kātyāyanīputra; Prakaraṇapāda – Vasumitra; Vijñānakāya – Devaśarman; Dharmaskandha – Śāriputra; Prajñaptiśāstra – Maudgalyāyana; Dhātukāya – Pūrṇa; Saṅgītiparyāya – Mahākauṣṭhila. Chinese attributions differ.

title: Saṅgītiparyāya
alt_titles: Apidamo jiyimen zu lun 阿毘達磨集異門足論 (T1536)

attribution.scholarly: Attribution to disciples of the Buddha is traditional; the works are dated by scholars to c. 3rd c. BCE – 1st c. CE

structure.description: 12 chapters following the numerical lists of the Saṅgīti-sūtra; 20 fascicles (Xuanzang)

summary: One of the six 'feet': a commentary on the Saṅgīti-sūtra (parallel to DN 33), arranging doctrines by number from one to ten.
notes: Yaśomitra's list (Sphuṭārthā on AK 1.3, checked locally): Jñānaprasthāna – Kātyāyanīputra; Prakaraṇapāda – Vasumitra; Vijñānakāya – Devaśarman; Dharmaskandha – Śāriputra; Prajñaptiśāstra – Maudgalyāyana; Dhātukāya – Pūrṇa; Saṅgītiparyāya – Mahākauṣṭhila. Chinese attributions differ.

title: Abhidharma-mahāvibhāṣā-śāstra
alt_titles: Apidamo da piposha lun 阿毘達磨大毘婆沙論 (T1545)

attribution.tradition: Compiled by five hundred arhats at a council convened by King Kaniṣka in Kashmir, with Vasumitra presiding and Pārśva as instigator (Xuanzang's Xiyu ji; Paramārtha's Life of Vasubandhu)
attribution.scholarly: A compilation of Kashmiri Sarvāstivāda exegesis, c. 2nd c. CE; its relation to Kaniṣka is doubted

tradition.text: Under King Kaniṣka, four hundred years after the parinirvāṇa

structure.description: 200 fascicles in Xuanzang's translation (656–659), commenting section by section on the Jñānaprasthāna and recording the views of the four great masters, Dārṣṭāntikas, Vibhajyavādins, Mahāsāṃghikas and others

summary: The great commentary on the Jñānaprasthāna and the authoritative text of the Kashmiri Vaibhāṣikas. It records the four masters' theories of existence in the three times, refutes the Dārṣṭāntikas, Vibhajyavādins and others, and gives the hostile Sarvāstivāda account of Mahādeva and the first schism.

title: Apitan piposha lun (*Abhidharma-vibhāṣā-śāstra)

structure.description: 60 fascicles surviving of 100; translated by Buddhavarman and Daotai, 437–439

summary: An earlier and shorter Chinese translation of a Vibhāṣā on the Jñānaprasthāna, partly lost.

title: Piposha lun (*Vibhāṣāśāstra) attributed to Śītapāṇi

structure.description: 14 fascicles; translated by Saṅghabhūti, 383

summary: A short early Vibhāṣā-type treatise, among the first Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma texts in Chinese.

title: Abhidharmahṛdaya
alt_titles: Apitan xin lun 阿毘曇心論 (T1550)

structure.description: Ten chapters of verses with prose; 4 fascicles (Saṅghadeva and Huiyuan, 391)

summary: The first verse digest of Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma, by Dharmaśrī (Dharmaśreṣṭhin), the model followed by the Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya and Vasubandhu's Kośa.

title: Abhidharmahṛdaya commentary of Upaśānta
alt_titles: Apitan xin lun jing 阿毘曇心論經 (T1551)

structure.description: 6 fascicles; translated by Narendrayaśas, 563

summary: Upaśānta's expanded commentary on Dharmaśrī's Abhidharmahṛdaya.

title: Saṃyuktābhidharmahṛdaya
alt_titles: Za apitan xin lun 雜阿毘曇心論 (T1552)

structure.description: 11 chapters; 11 fascicles; translated by Saṅghavarman and others, 434

summary: Dharmatrāta's enlarged Abhidharmahṛdaya incorporating Vibhāṣā material; the direct predecessor of the Abhidharmakośa in plan.

title: Abhidharmāmṛtarasa
alt_titles: Apitan ganlu wei lun 阿毘曇甘露味論 (T1553)

structure.description: 16 chapters; 2 fascicles

summary: A short Abhidharma compendium attributed to Ghoṣaka, covering giving and morality, the realms, karma, the path and meditation.

title: Abhidharmakośa (Abhidharmakośakārikā)
alt_titles: Apidamo jushe lun 阿毘達磨俱舍論

attribution.tradition: Composed by Vasubandhu of Puruṣapura, who studied the Vibhāṣā in Kashmir and later turned to the Mahāyāna under Asaṅga (Paramārtha's Life of Vasubandhu; Xuanzang)
attribution.scholarly: Vasubandhu, c. 4th–5th c. CE; whether the Kośa's author and the Yogācāra author are the same person has been debated

structure.description: Eight chapters (kośasthāna) of verses — 1 elements (dhātu), 2 faculties (indriya), 3 the world (loka), 4 action (karma), 5 latent defilements (anuśaya), 6 the path and persons (mārga-pudgala), 7 knowledge (jñāna), 8 meditative attainments (samāpatti) — c. 600 verses (597 numbered in the GRETIL e-text); a ninth, prose chapter on the refutation of the person (pudgala-viniścaya) belongs to the bhāṣya

summary: Vasubandhu's verse summary of Sarvāstivāda-Vaibhāṣika Abhidharma: the analysis of dharmas into aggregates, sense-bases and elements; the faculties, mental factors, dissociated factors, causes and conditions; cosmology, rebirth and dependent origination; karma and vows; the latent defilements; the path of seeing and cultivation and the noble persons; the knowledges and the Buddha's qualities; and the meditative attainments. It closes by describing its Abhidharma as mostly that of the Kashmiri Vaibhāṣikas (8.40).

editions.name: Abhidharmakośakārikā, GRETIL e-text (after Pradhan 1967/1975 and Gokhale 1946)
Paramārtha, T1559 (563–567); Xuanzang, T1558 (651–654); Tibetan D4089
L. de La Vallée Poussin, L'Abhidharmakośa de Vasubandhu (French, 1923–1931)

title: Abhidharmakośabhāṣya

attribution.tradition: Vasubandhu's own commentary, in which he states the Vaibhāṣika position and often criticizes it from the Sautrāntika side

structure.description: Prose commentary on the eight chapters plus the ninth chapter, 'pudgala-viniścaya' (Pradhan pp. 461–479). Sanskrit manuscript found by Rāhula Sāṅkṛtyāyana in Tibet (1930s), ed. P. Pradhan 1967, rev. 1975.

summary: The prose auto-commentary to the Kośa. It reports the Vaibhāṣika positions (often marked with 'kila', 'so they say') and argues the Sautrāntika alternatives: seeds instead of possession, the present alone as existent, causeless destruction, the unreality of avijñapti and of the unconditioned. Its ninth chapter refutes the Vātsīputrīya person and the non-Buddhist self.

title: Sphuṭārthā Abhidharmakośavyākhyā
summary: Yaśomitra's complete Sanskrit sub-commentary on the Kośa and bhāṣya, from a Sautrāntika standpoint. It lists the authors of the seven Abhidharma books, defines the Sautrāntikas as those who take the sūtras, not the treatises, as authority, and identifies many opponents of the bhāṣya.

title: Nyāyānusāra
alt_titles: Shun zhengli lun 順正理論 (T1562)
*Kośakarakā ('hailstone on the Kośa', its first title per Xuanzang)

structure.description: 80 fascicles (Xuanzang, 653–654); comments on the Kośa's verses (without chapter 9) and refutes the bhāṣya's Sautrāntika positions

summary: Saṅghabhadra's massive defence of Vaibhāṣika orthodoxy against Vasubandhu's bhāṣya, preserving the views of the Sautrāntika Śrīlāta and others.

title: Abhidharmasamayapradīpikā
alt_titles: Apidamo xianzong lun 阿毘達磨藏顯宗論 (T1563)

structure.description: 40 fascicles (Xuanzang, 651–652)

summary: Saṅghabhadra's shorter positive exposition of Vaibhāṣika doctrine.

title: Abhidharmāvatāra
alt_titles: Ru apidamo lun 入阿毘達磨論 (T1554)

structure.description: 2 fascicles (Xuanzang, 658); organized by the five groups/eight categories of dharmas

summary: Skandhila's concise introduction to Vaibhāṣika Abhidharma.

title: Abhidharmadīpa with Vibhāṣāprabhāvṛtti

attribution.tradition: Anonymous author ('Dīpakāra'); the GRETIL file names Vimalamitra
attribution.scholarly: An orthodox Vaibhāṣika reply to the Kośa, c. 5th–6th c.; author unknown

summary: A Vaibhāṣika verse treatise with auto-commentary that follows the Kośa's plan while attacking Vasubandhu ('the Kośakāra') as leaning to the Sautrāntika and Mahāyāna.

title: Abhidharmakośopāyikā-ṭīkā
summary: Śamathadeva's collection, in Tibetan, of the sūtra passages cited in the Kośa, preserving many (Mūla)sarvāstivāda Āgama sūtras in full; a key witness for Āgama parallels.

title: Karmasiddhiprakaraṇa
alt_titles: las grub pa'i rab tu byed pa (D4062)
Dasheng chengye lun 大乘成業論 (T1609)
summary: Vasubandhu's treatise establishing karma: it rejects shape and avijñapti as bodily action, treats action as volition, and explains the continuity of karma through the transformation of the series and a store-consciousness.

title: Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa
summary: Vasubandhu's short analysis of the five aggregates; Yaśomitra cites it for Vasubandhu's own definition of vitarka and vicāra as varieties of volition and wisdom.

title: Śāriputrābhidharma
alt_titles: Shelifu apitan lun 舍利弗阿毘曇論 (T1548)

attribution.scholarly: Often assigned to the Dharmaguptaka (or another Vibhajyavāda school); c. 1st c. BCE–2nd c. CE

structure.description: 30 fascicles; translated by Dharmayaśas and Dharmagupta, 407–414

summary: A non-Sarvāstivāda Abhidharma in four parts, sharing material with the Pali Vibhaṅga and Puggalapaññatti.

title: Kalpanāmaṇḍitikā Dṛṣṭāntapaṅkti
alt_titles: Da zhuangyan lun jing 大莊嚴論經 (T201, ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa)

attribution.tradition: The Chinese version is ascribed to Aśvaghoṣa
attribution.scholarly: Sanskrit fragments from Kizil (ed. Lüders 1926) name Kumāralāta as author

summary: A collection of edifying stories and examples (dṛṣṭānta) illustrating the Dharma, associated with the Dārṣṭāntika teachers.

editions.name: Lüders, Bruchstücke der Kalpanāmaṇḍitikā (1926), GRETIL e-text

title: Satyasiddhiśāstra

attribution.tradition: Harivarman, a pupil in the Sarvāstivāda who departed from it
attribution.scholarly: c. 3rd–4th c. CE; school affiliation (Sautrāntika, Bahuśrutīya) debated

structure.description: 202 chapters in five sections (the Jewels; the truth of suffering; of origin; of cessation; of the path); 16 fascicles (Kumārajīva, 411–412). Sanskrit retranslation by N. Aiyaswami Sastri (Baroda 1975).

summary: Harivarman's 'establishment of the truth', which organizes Abhidharma around the four truths, rejects the Sarvāstivāda's three-time existence and many real entities, and teaches the emptiness of persons and of dharmas; the basis of the Chinese Chengshi school.

title: Samayabhedoparacanacakra
alt_titles: Yibu zonglun lun 異部宗輪論 (T2031, Xuanzang)
Shiba bu lun 十八部論 (T2032)
Bu zhi yi lun 部執異論 (T2033, Paramārtha)
gzhung tha dad pa rim par klag pa'i 'khor lo (D4138)
The Wheel of the Formation of the Differing Doctrines

attribution.tradition: Vasumitra, four hundred years after the parinirvāṇa
attribution.scholarly: A Sarvāstivāda doxography, c. 1st–3rd c. CE; whether its author is the Vibhāṣā master is doubted

structure.description: An account of the first schism (over Mahādeva's five points, under Aśoka), the successive divisions into twenty groups (9 Mahāsāṃghika, 11 Sthavira), and the 'root' and 'derived' tenets of each

summary: The principal Indian doxography of the early schools. It narrates the first schism over the five points of Mahādeva, lists the schools that arose in the second to fourth centuries after the parinirvāṇa, and records their tenets on the Buddha, the arhat, the three times, the intermediate existence, the person and the unconditioned.

title: Nikāyabhedavibhaṅgavyākhyāna
alt_titles: sde pa tha dad par byed pa dang rnam par bshad pa (D4139)

attribution.scholarly: Related to chapter 4 of the Tarkajvālā; identity of the author debated

summary: A doxography giving several different accounts of the division into eighteen schools (one of them according to the Saṃmitīyas) and summarizing their tenets.

title: Samayabhedoparacanacakre Nikāyabhedopadeśanasaṃgraha
summary: Vinītadeva's summary of the eighteen schools arranged in four groups — Sarvāstivāda (Mūla-sarvāstivāda, Kāśyapīya, Mahīśāsaka, Dharmaguptaka, Bahuśrutīya, Tāmraśāṭīya, Vibhajyavāda), Mahāsāṃghika (Pūrvaśaila, Aparaśaila, Haimavata, Lokottaravāda, Prajñaptivāda), Saṃmitīya (Kaurukullaka, Āvantaka, Vātsīputrīya) and Sthavira (Jetavanīya, Abhayagirivāsin, Mahāvihāravāsin) — the classification followed in Tibet (low confidence on the exact membership).

title: Śāriputraparipṛcchā
alt_titles: Shelifu wen jing 舍利弗問經 (T1465)
summary: A Mahāsāṃghika-affiliated text in which the first schism is explained by an elder's enlargement of the Vinaya, the Mahāsāṃghikas keeping the original recension.

title: Dīpavaṃsa

structure.description: 22 chapters of verse; ch. 5 narrates the councils and the schisms

summary: The oldest Sri Lankan chronicle. Its fifth chapter tells how the Vajjiputtakas defeated at the Second Council formed the Mahāsaṅgītika and lists the eighteen schools (six Mahāsaṅgītika branches, twelve Theravāda branches) and six later ones.

title: Mahāvaṃsa
summary: The great Sri Lankan chronicle; chapters 4–5 narrate the Second and Third Councils and the eighteen schools, and the Buddha as a 'vibhajjavādī'.

title: Kathāvatthu-aṭṭhakathā
summary: The commentary on the Kathāvatthu, which assigns each refuted view to named schools (Puggalavādins — Vajjiputtakas and Sammitiyas; Sabbatthivādins; Andhakas; Pubbaseliyas; Uttarāpathakas; Vetulyakas; and others).

title: Da Tang Xiyu ji
summary: Xuanzang's record of his journey, noting for many monasteries the number of monks and their school (Sarvāstivāda, Saṃmitīya, Mahāsāṃghika, Lokottaravāda, Sthavira) and relating the Kashmir council under Kaniṣka.

title: Nanhai jigui neifa zhuan
alt_titles: A Record of the Inner Law Sent Home from the Southern Seas
summary: Yijing's account of Indian monastic practice according to the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, describing four principal nikāyas — Mahāsāṃghika, Sthavira, Mūlasarvāstivāda and Saṃmitīya — and their regional distribution.

title: Tāranātha's History of Buddhism in India
summary: Tāranātha's history of Indian Buddhism, including traditional accounts of the councils and the divisions into eighteen schools.

title: Dharmaguptaka Vinaya (Four-Part Vinaya)

structure.description: 60 fascicles in four parts: bhikṣu-vibhaṅga, bhikṣuṇī-vibhaṅga, the skandhakas, and supplements; 250 rules for bhikṣus, 348 for bhikṣuṇīs

summary: The Vinaya of the Dharmaguptaka, the living monastic code of Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese and Taiwanese Buddhism, preserving full ordination for both monks and nuns.

title: Dharmaguptaka Prātimokṣa (Sifen seng jieben)
summary: The recitation text of the 250 bhikṣu rules (and the 348 bhikṣuṇī rules in the nuns' version) recited at the fortnightly poṣadha in East Asia.

title: Mahīśāsaka Vinaya (Five-Part Vinaya)

scholarly.text: translated 423–424 CE from a manuscript Faxian obtained in Sri Lanka

structure.description: 30 fascicles in five parts

summary: The Vinaya of the Mahīśāsaka, translated by Buddhajīva with Zhu Daosheng.

title: Mahāsāṃghika Vinaya
alt_titles: Mohe sengqi lü 摩訶僧祇律 (T1425)

scholarly.text: translated 416–418 CE from a manuscript Faxian obtained at Pāṭaliputra

structure.description: 40 fascicles; 218 bhikṣu rules (moderate confidence on the count)

summary: The Vinaya of the Mahāsāṃghika, including its own account of the councils.

title: Sarvāstivāda Vinaya (Ten-Recitation Vinaya)

scholarly.text: translated 404–409 CE (Puṇyatāra, Kumārajīva; completed by Dharmaruci and Vimalākṣa)

structure.description: 61 fascicles in ten recitations (adhyāya)

summary: The Vinaya of the Sarvāstivāda, the first complete Vinaya translated into Chinese.

title: Prātimokṣasūtra of the Sarvāstivādins

structure.description: 263 bhikṣu rules (low confidence on the total)

summary: The Sanskrit recitation text of the Sarvāstivāda monk's rules, reconstructed from Turfan manuscripts.

title: Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya
alt_titles: Genben shuo yiqie you bu pinaiye 根本說一切有部毘奈耶 (T1442–1451)

scholarly.text: compiled c. 1st–4th c. CE; Chinese translation 703–710 (Yijing); Tibetan c. 800 CE

structure.description: Vinayavastu (17 vastus), Prātimokṣasūtra, Vinayavibhaṅga, Bhikṣuṇī texts, Kṣudrakavastu, Uttaragrantha (in the Tibetan arrangement: four scriptures)

summary: The largest surviving Vinaya, full of narratives; the monastic code of Tibetan Buddhism.

title: Vinayavastu (Mūlasarvāstivāda)

structure.description: 17 sections: pravrajyā, poṣadha, pravāraṇā, varṣā, carma, bhaiṣajya, cīvara, kaṭhina, kauśāmbaka, karma, pāṇḍulohitaka, pudgala, pārivāsika, poṣadhasthāpana, śayanāsana, adhikaraṇa, saṅghabheda

summary: The seventeen 'sections' governing ordination, the fortnightly observance, the rains, robes, medicines, legal acts, probation and schism; much survives in the Gilgit manuscripts.

editions.name: N. Dutt, Gilgit Manuscripts III (1942–50); GRETIL e-texts of several vastus

title: Saṅghabhedavastu
summary: The seventeenth and last section of the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinayavastu: a long life of the Buddha from the origin of the world and the Śākyas to Devadatta's schism.

title: Prātimokṣasūtra of the Mūlasarvāstivādins
summary: The recitation text of the Mūlasarvāstivāda monk's rules, recited in Tibetan monasteries.

editions.name: A. C. Banerjee (1954; Gilgit manuscript), GRETIL e-text

title: Prātimokṣasūtra of the Mahāsāṃghikas
summary: The Mahāsāṃghika monk's rules in Sanskrit.

editions.name: W. Pachow and R. Mishra (Allahabad 1956), GRETIL e-text

title: Prātimokṣasūtra of the Lokottaravāda-Mahāsāṃghikas
summary: The Lokottaravāda monk's rules in Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit.

title: Bhikṣuṇī-Vinaya of the Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda
summary: The nuns' Vinaya of the Lokottaravāda, including the eight weighty rules and the nuns' offences.

title: Abhisamācārikā Dharmāḥ
summary: The Lokottaravāda rules of monastic etiquette and daily conduct.

editions.name: Taishō University study group digital edition, GRETIL

title: Kāśyapīya Prātimokṣa
alt_titles: Jietuo jie jing 解脫戒經 (T1460)
summary: The only surviving Kāśyapīya Vinaya text.

title: Vinayasūtra
summary: Guṇaprabha's digest of the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya in aphorisms; one of the five great texts of the Tibetan monastic curriculum.

title: Vinaya-dvāviṃśati-prasannārtha-śāstra
alt_titles: Lü ershier mingliao lun 律二十二明了論 (T1461)
summary: A short Saṃmitīya Vinaya treatise attributed to Buddhatrāta, the only Saṃmitīya Vinaya text known (low confidence).

title: Mahāvastu

attribution.tradition: The beginning of the Mahāvastu of the Vinaya Piṭaka according to the recitation of the Lokottaravādin Mahāsāṃghikas of the Middle Country (colophon, Mvu i.2)
attribution.scholarly: A compilation grown over centuries, c. 2nd c. BCE – 4th c. CE

structure.description: Three volumes in Senart's edition: the hells and other worlds; the four conducts and ten grounds (bhūmi) of the bodhisattva; Dīpaṅkara; the birth, renunciation and awakening; the first sermon and the first converts; many jātakas and avadānas

summary: The Lokottaravāda's vast biography of the Buddha within its Vinaya, teaching the supramundane Buddha who only conforms to the world, the four conducts and ten grounds of the bodhisattva, and containing the first sermon and other parallels to the Pali and Āgama texts.

title: Lokānuvartana-sūtra
alt_titles: Neizang baibao jing 內藏百寶經 (T807)
'jig rten gyi rjes su mthun par 'jug pa'i mdo
summary: A sūtra teaching that the Buddha only appears to conform to worldly life (eating, washing, ageing) while being beyond the world; associated with the Pūrvaśaila (low confidence on the affiliation).

title: Dīrghāgama (Chinese)
alt_titles: Chang ahan jing 長阿含經 (T1)

structure.description: 22 fascicles, 30 sūtras in four sections

summary: The Chinese 'long discourses', affiliated with the Dharmaguptaka, parallel to the Pali Dīgha Nikāya (e.g. DĀ 2 Yu xing jing ↔ DN 16; DĀ 21 Fandong jing ↔ DN 1; DĀ 27 ↔ DN 2).

title: Madhyamāgama (Chinese)
alt_titles: Zhong ahan jing 中阿含經 (T26)

structure.description: 60 fascicles, 222 sūtras in 18 chapters

summary: The Chinese 'middle-length discourses' of the Sarvāstivāda, parallel to the Majjhima Nikāya and parts of the Aṅguttara (e.g. MĀ 98 Nianchu jing ↔ MN 10; MĀ 81 ↔ MN 119; MĀ 16 ↔ AN 3.65).

title: Saṃyuktāgama (Chinese)
alt_titles: Za ahan jing 雜阿含經 (T99)

scholarly.text: translated 435–443 CE from a manuscript Faxian brought from Sri Lanka

structure.description: 50 fascicles, 1362 sūtras in the Taishō numbering (the order of the fascicles is disturbed; reconstructed by Lü Cheng and Yinshun)

summary: The Chinese 'connected discourses', affiliated with the (Mūla)sarvāstivāda, parallel to the Saṃyutta Nikāya (e.g. SĀ 379 ↔ SN 56.11; SĀ 34 ↔ SN 22.59; SĀ 301 ↔ SN 12.15).

title: Bieyi Za ahan jing (the 'other' Saṃyuktāgama)

structure.description: 16 fascicles, 364 sūtras; translator unknown

summary: A partial Saṃyuktāgama of a school other than that of T99, sometimes attributed to the Kāśyapīya (scholarly hypothesis).

title: Za ahan jing (single-fascicle Saṃyuktāgama)

structure.description: 1 fascicle, 27 sūtras; early translation, translator uncertain

summary: A small early collection of Saṃyukta-type sūtras.

title: Ekottarikāgama (Chinese)
alt_titles: Zengyi ahan jing 增壹阿含經 (T125)

scholarly.text: translated 384–385 CE (revision by Saṅghadeva, 397, has been proposed)

structure.description: 51 fascicles, 52 chapters, 472 sūtras arranged by number from one to eleven

summary: The Chinese 'numerical discourses', parallel to the Aṅguttara Nikāya; its school affiliation is debated (Mahāsāṃghika, Dharmaguptaka and Sarvāstivāda have been proposed) and it contains some Mahāyāna elements.
notes: lineages lists Mahāsāṃghika only as the most-cited proposal.

title: Dīrghāgama (Sanskrit, Gilgit manuscript)

structure.description: About 47 sūtras in three sections; a large part of one birch-bark manuscript surfaced in the 1990s

summary: The (Mūla)sarvāstivāda long discourses in Sanskrit, parallel to the Dīgha Nikāya and the Chinese Dīrghāgama.

title: Nidānasaṃyukta (Sanskrit)
summary: Twenty-five sūtras on dependent origination from a Sanskrit Saṃyuktāgama found at Turfan, parallel to the Pali Nidāna Saṃyutta.

title: Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra (Sanskrit, Sarvāstivāda)
summary: The Sanskrit account of the Buddha's last journey and parinirvāṇa, parallel to DN 16 and DĀ 2.

title: Mahāvadānasūtra
summary: The Sanskrit sūtra on the seven past Buddhas and the life of Vipaśyin, parallel to DN 14 and DĀ 1.

title: Catuṣpariṣatsūtra
summary: The Sanskrit sūtra of the founding of the four assemblies — the awakening, the first sermon and the first conversions — parallel to Vinaya Mahāvagga 1 and the Mahāvastu.

title: Arthapada-sūtra (Chinese)
summary: The Chinese parallel to the Pali Aṭṭhakavagga of the Sutta Nipāta, with a prose frame story for each poem.

title: Faju jing (Chinese Dharmapada)

scholarly.text: translated 224 CE by Wei Qinan and others

structure.description: 39 chapters, c. 750 verses

summary: The earliest Chinese Dharmapada, combining a core close to the Pali Dhammapada with additional chapters.

title: The Gāndhārī Buddhist manuscripts

structure.description: Birch-bark scrolls and fragments in several collections: the British Library, the Senior collection, the Bajaur collection, the Schøyen and other collections; the Khotan Dharmapada found earlier

summary: The oldest surviving Buddhist manuscripts, in the Gāndhārī language: sūtras with Pali and Āgama parallels, Dharmapada verses, the Rhinoceros Sūtra, Abhidharma and commentary texts, avadānas, Prātimokṣa and early Mahāyāna sūtras.

title: British Library Kharoṣṭhī fragments

structure.description: About 29 fragments of birch-bark scrolls found in a clay pot whose inscription names the Dharmaguptakas

summary: The collection that opened Gāndhārī studies: Dharmapada-type verses, the Rhinoceros Sūtra, Ekottarikāgama-type sūtras, a commentary on the Saṃgīti-sūtra, Abhidharma, avadānas and the Anavatapta verses.

title: Senior collection of Gāndhārī scrolls

structure.description: About two dozen scrolls, largely in one hand, found in an inscribed pot

summary: A collection consisting mostly of sūtras with Saṃyutta/Saṃyuktāgama parallels, and the Anavatapta verses.

title: Bajaur collection of Gāndhārī manuscripts
summary: Some nineteen scrolls from Bajaur (Pakistan), including a Prātimokṣa, karmavācanā material and an early Mahāyāna sūtra connected with the buddha Akṣobhya.

title: Schøyen collection Buddhist manuscripts (Bamiyan finds)
summary: Thousands of fragments said to come from the Bamiyan area, including Mahāsāṃghika-Lokottaravāda Vinaya fragments, Āgama sūtras and early Mahāyāna sūtras (low confidence on the contents).

title: Gāndhārī Dharmapada (Khotan manuscript)

scholarly.text: found near Khotan 1892; c. 2nd c. CE

summary: A birch-bark Dharmapada in Gāndhārī, divided between Paris and St Petersburg and edited by John Brough (1962); its chapters overlap with the Pali Dhammapada, the Udānavarga and the Patna Dharmapada.

title: Gāndhārī Rhinoceros Sūtra
summary: The Gāndhārī version of the Khaggavisāṇa-sutta (Sutta Nipāta 1.3), 'wander alone like the rhinoceros', edited by Richard Salomon (2000).

title: Gilgit manuscripts

scholarly.text: found 1931 (and 1938) at Naupur near Gilgit; manuscripts c. 5th–7th c. CE

summary: Birch-bark manuscripts from a stūpa near Gilgit: the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, the Dharmaskandha, Ekottarāgama fragments, a Dīrghāgama and Mahāyāna sūtras (Lotus, Samādhirāja, Vajracchedikā, Bhaiṣajyaguru). Edited by Nalinaksha Dutt; facsimiles by Raghu Vira and Lokesh Chandra.

title: Sanskrit manuscripts from the Turfan finds

scholarly.text: recovered 1902–1914 by the Prussian expeditions; c. 3rd–10th c. CE

summary: Fragments from Chinese Turkestan (Turfan, Kucha) of the Sarvāstivāda canon — Āgama sūtras, Prātimokṣa, Vinaya, Abhidharma, Udānavarga — published in the series Sanskrithandschriften aus den Turfanfunden.

title: Udānavarga

attribution.tradition: Arranged in chapters by the elder Dharmatrāta (Yaśomitra, Sphuṭārthā on AK 1.3)
attribution.scholarly: The Sarvāstivāda Dharmapada, c. 1st–4th c. CE

structure.description: 33 chapters (varga), about a thousand verses

summary: The Sarvāstivāda counterpart of the Dhammapada, enlarged with verses parallel to other Pali collections; preserved in Sanskrit (Turfan), Tibetan and Chinese.

title: Patna Dharmapada

structure.description: 22 chapters, c. 414 verses

summary: A Dharmapada in a Prakrit-like language from a manuscript photographed in Tibet by Rāhula Sāṅkṛtyāyana; its school has been proposed to be the Saṃmitīya (scholarly hypothesis).

title: Divyāvadāna
summary: A collection of thirty-eight narratives, many drawn from the Mūlasarvāstivāda Vinaya, including the Aśokāvadāna.

title: Aśokāvadāna
summary: The legend of King Aśoka and the elder Upagupta of Mathurā, with the Sarvāstivāda succession of masters (Mahākāśyapa, Ānanda, Śāṇakavāsin, Upagupta).

title: Saṃmitīyanikāya-śāstra
alt_titles: Sanmidi bu lun 三彌底部論 (T1649)

scholarly.text: Chinese translation, translator unknown, c. 385–431 CE

structure.description: 3 fascicles

summary: A Saṃmitīya treatise that argues against views denying the person and sets out the person as designated on the basis of support, transmigration and cessation (low confidence on the terms).

title: Tridharmaka-śāstra
alt_titles: San fadu lun 三法度論 (T1506)
Si ahan muchao jie 四阿鋡暮抄解 (T1505, earlier version)

attribution.tradition: Ascribed to Vasubhadra, with a commentary by Saṅghasena (low confidence)

summary: A manual organized in triads (virtue, vice and dependence; each in three and three) considered Pudgalavāda; translated by Gautama Saṅghadeva in 391.

title: Sifen lü shanfan buque xingshi chao
alt_titles: 四分律刪繁補闕行事鈔 (T1804)
summary: Daoxuan's practical commentary on the Four-Part Vinaya, the foundation of the Nanshan Vinaya school.
